figures.caption: Fig. 1: Brain2Face. (Left) A 64-channel EEG recording is encoded into a pre-trained latent expression of a Gaussian avatar prior (Teotia et al., 2025). Then, the frozen decoder of this prior takes the predicted expression and a subject-specific identity latent and regresses Gaussian splat parameters and geometry. We note that acquiring the identity latent requires a personalization step. (Right) Fitted targets for six participants (rows) and four expressions (columns) of our newly acquired dataset.
Fig. 2: Overview of the Brain2Face dataset. Our dataset comprises paired EEG and multi-view video data covering multiple facial expressions, views, and subjects.

Fig. 3: Qualitative reconstruction of seen and unseen expression types. Each row shows one subject, with Ours and Ground truth paired for each expression group. Ground truth denotes the fitted Gaussian-avatar render at the matching frame.

Fig. 4: Brain2Face overview. A synchronized recording segment aligns annotated multi-view video with preprocessed (Sec. 4.1) EEG. Expression groups are assigned to training and test sets (Tab. 6) before windows are sampled. Offline UHAP avatar fitting produces the subject identity code Zid; a frozen image encoder produces the expression trajectory Zexp, which is the direct regression target for the EEG encoder E (frozen or fine-tuned) and decoder M. Consecutive EEG windows are processed with shared weights, and their predicted chunks are concatenated into a continuous latent sequence Ẑexp, which drives the frozen UHAP decoder DUHAP. Latent loss Lp compares the prediction against the target expression codes. Mesh and landmark losses Lv and Lℓ supervise decoded geometry and backpropagate through the frozen avatar decoder, the EEG-to-expression decoder M and, when unfrozen, the EEG encoder are updated. The auxiliary loss Laux (Sec. 4.2) is omitted for clarity.

Fig. 5: Per-subject Gaussian-avatar fitting and inversion. Calibrated multi-view expression frames provide RGB images and foreground masks. Sapiens landmarks are triangulated and mapped to canonical coordinates to form pose-free 3D guide points. Teotia et al. introduced both the UHAP prior and the gaze-conditioned image encoder used here Teotia et al. (2025). For each frame, the frozen encoder produces an expression code Zt exp ∈ Rd, where d = 256. Fitting adapts the participant’s identity code Zid ∈ R512 and the avatar decoder weights ΦUHAP, together with pose and color calibration, using the multi-view images and 3D guides. The fitting loss includes mouth and regularization terms; Sec. A.3 describes these terms. After the final guide-mesh refinement, the fitted decoder weights ΦUHAP and identity Zid are frozen. The saved expression trajectory Zexp provides the target for EEG-to-expression regression. Predicted expression codes then drive the frozen personalized avatar.
